scout.purpose: External observable data must become Compose State without wasting resources or publishing updates to an inactive destination.
scout.realWorldUse: Repository Flow, screen UiState, saved arguments, and one-off operations meet Compose at the route boundary.
scout.outcome: Expose immutable StateFlow, collect with lifecycle awareness, choose an initial state, and retain screen ownership correctly.

blocks.text: A ViewModel is a screen-level state holder that survives configuration changes and owns business work for its scope. It commonly exposes immutable StateFlow UiState created by mapping and combining repositories, SavedStateHandle arguments, and user events. stateIn can share upstream work and provide an initial value. The ViewModel should not hold Activity, View, NavController, or composable references. It also does not replace durable persistence: it rebuilds screen state from repositories and compact saved keys.

blocks.caption: The Android-aware route collects; reusable content receives plain data and intent.

blocks.text: On Android, collectAsStateWithLifecycle collects a Flow and exposes Compose State while respecting the host lifecycle, stopping collection below the configured active state. This avoids keeping UI-only upstream work active while the destination is stopped. collectAsState is suitable where Android lifecycle integration is not available or for platform-independent code with a separately defined lifecycle. LiveData and Rx types have adapters, but the state owner should still expose one coherent contract rather than mixing observables per field.

blocks.title: Collect at the route
blocks.text: Keep Android lifecycle and state-holder lookup outside reusable content.

sections.title: Route and content have different jobs

blocks.text: The route retrieves or receives the ViewModel, collects its UiState, and converts navigation or snackbar outputs at the boundary. The content composable receives immutable state and callbacks. Represent loading, content, empty, and failure explicitly; do not use null ambiguously for all of them. One-off events require a delivery contract and should not be encoded as a permanent Boolean that retriggers after collection. Test the ViewModel as ordinary Kotlin state transformation and test content with supplied snapshots.

A production implementation should make this topic observable and testable. Start with a concrete user outcome, then cover loading or absence, failure, recreation, rapid repeated input, long content, large font scale, and alternate navigation entry where relevant. Keep state ownership visible in parameters and keep side effects behind a lifecycle-aware boundary. Use previews for representative visual states, unit tests for pure state transformation, Compose UI tests for semantics and interaction, and runtime inspection only when the question depends on scheduling, layout, drawing, or device behaviour. Document any trade-off that a future maintainer cannot infer from the code. Correctness means the feature still behaves predictably when recomposition, cancellation, configuration change, or user timing differs from the happy-path demonstration.

trap_check.mistake: Storing Activity or NavController in a ViewModel.
trap_check.why: The owner outlives configuration instances and couples state logic to UI runtime.
trap_check.fix: Emit state or intent and perform navigation at the route boundary.

trap_check.mistake: Optimising or abstracting before the behaviour is measured.
trap_check.why: It adds machinery while the actual ownership or runtime problem remains unknown.
trap_check.fix: Write a focused test or collect runtime evidence before changing the design.

challenge_intro.task: Create repository Flow, ViewModel StateFlow, a lifecycle-aware route, and stateless content with explicit loading, empty, error, and content states.
challenge_intro.successLooksLike: Upstream data has one immutable screen contract. Inactive destination collection follows lifecycle policy. Content previews cover every state without a ViewModel.

recall.answer: Screen state and business work for its scope.
